output.answer:
I can't say for sure yet, because the fix depends on how you send traces. **How are you tracing: the Python SDK, the TypeScript SDK, OpenTelemetry (OTel, an open tracing standard), or an agent plugin? And which view are you checking, Traces or Agents?** Each setup fails in different ways.

In the meantime, these are the most common causes:

- **`weave.init()` was never called.** Weave only traces calls to supported LLM libraries (such as `openai` or `anthropic`) after you import the library and initialize your project with `weave.init('your-project')` [S5].
- **Your own functions aren't marked for tracing.** To trace custom code, decorate it with `@weave.op` in Python or wrap it with `weave.op(...)` in TypeScript. You can also create Calls manually through the API [S1].
- **The program exits before traces are sent.** Weave sends data in the background. In TypeScript, await `client.flush()` before `process.exit()` [S3]. In Python, `flush()` finishes background tasks and is safe to call more than once [S6].
- **TypeScript automatic tracing isn't working.** Projects that use ES modules (ESM), bundlers such as Next.js, or restricted runtimes can stop Weave from attaching to libraries automatically. The integration guide's troubleshooting section covers fixes [S4].
- **OTel spans are going to a different view.** The older OTel endpoint feeds the **Traces** and **Threads** views, and OpenInference spans sent there appear in **Traces**, not **Agents**. The Agents view builds conversations from spans that follow the OTel GenAI semantic conventions (a standard naming scheme for AI spans), sent to the agents endpoint [S2]. Also check that your entity (team name), project and `wandb-api-key` header are set. In TypeScript, call `provider.shutdown()` before exit so pending spans get sent [S2].

Tell me your setup and I'll narrow it down.

# Trace your code

> Instrument your running code so its execution appears as detailed traces in Weave.

This guide shows you how to instrument your application so that its execution appears as detailed traces in Weave. Traces help you debug, evaluate, and monitor LLM-powered code by capturing inputs, outputs, and the structure of each operation as a Call.

* Automatic tracking of LLM library calls.
* Tracking of custom functions with `weave.op`.
* Manual Call tracking using the API directly.

Choose the approach that fits how much control you need over what gets traced.

# Send OpenTelemetry Traces to Weave

> Import OpenTelemetry compatible trace data through a dedicated endpoint

> [!WARNING]
>
> This page documents W\&B Weave's legacy OTel workflow. If you are new to Weave and are building agentic applications, we **highly recommend** [sending your traces to the new endpoint](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-otel.md), `/agents/otel/v1/traces`. The new endpoint lets you send OTLP trace data from any OpenTelemetry pipeline to both W\&B Weave and [Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/what-is-agent-lens.md), an agent-focused tracing and observability platform.

Weave supports import of OpenTelemetry compatible trace data through a dedicated endpoint. This endpoint lets you send OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) formatted trace data directly to your Weave project. Use this integration when you want to instrument your application with the OpenTelemetry standard and have those traces appear alongside your other Weave data, without replacing your existing OTel-based observability pipeline.

This page covers the endpoint details, authentication, end-to-end examples in Python and TypeScript, how to forward traces through an OpenTelemetry Collector, how to organize traces into Weave threads, and the attribute mappings Weave applies to incoming spans.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This endpoint feeds the **Traces** and **Threads** views. To send OTel spans from a multi-turn agent to the **Agents** view, use the agents endpoint instead. See [Send OpenTelemetry spans to the Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-otel.md).

> ```
>

### Instrument and trace functions

To trace individual function calls, application code, or custom logic, use Weave Ops and Calls. Add one line to any function to track inputs, outputs, cost, token count, and latency. You can also:

* Track end-to-end how data flows through your LLM application.
* See source documents used to produce the LLM feedback.
* Drill down into specific prompts and how answers are produced.

To trace individual functions, follow the Weave [Op tracing quickstart](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/quickstart.md) or learn to use the Weave [Ops and Calls](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md).

# W&B Weave

> Track, test, and improve language model apps with W&B Weave

W\&B Weave is an observability and evaluation platform that helps you track, evaluate, and improve your agents and LLM applications. With Weave, you can:

# Trace your code

> Instrument your running code so its execution appears as detailed traces in Weave.

This guide shows you how to instrument your application so that its execution appears as detailed traces in Weave. Traces help you debug, evaluate, and monitor LLM-powered code by capturing inputs, outputs, and the structure of each operation as a Call.

To see your running code as detailed traces in Weave, you create Calls. The following sections describe the three main ways to do this, from least to most manual:

* Automatic tracking of LLM library calls.
* Tracking of custom functions with `weave.op`.
* Manual Call tracking using the API directly.

Choose the approach that fits how much control you need over what gets traced.

In the meantime, these are the most common causes:

- **TypeScript automatic tracing isn't working.** Projects that use ES modules (ESM), bundlers such as Next.js, or restricted runtimes can stop Weave from attaching to libraries automatically. The integration guide's troubleshooting section covers fixes [S4].
- **OTel spans are going to a different view.** Spans sent to the older OTel endpoint, including OpenInference spans, appear under **Traces**, not **Agents**. For the Agents view, use the `/agents/otel/v1/traces` endpoint [S2]. Also check that your entity (team name), project and `wandb-api-key` header are set. In TypeScript, call `provider.shutdown()` before exit so pending spans get sent [S2].
